items.item_text: Is exposed to excessive noise: Yes
Is exposed to marked changes in temperature and/or humidity: Yes

Other: Ability to work in machine room environments, which may be hot/cold, dirty and have poor connectivity. • Must be able to adjust schedule as campus needs require, identify major building equipment components and follow all safety processes and protocols.
Minimum of 6 years of related experience.

Deferred Maintenance Remediation & Project Coordination - Manage and support capital backlog projects funding through ICAMP allocation programs. Track complex repair work, analyze technical documents, and coordinate major system priorities (e.g., chillers, boilers, roofing, switchgear) with internal trade shops, PD&C and external contractors. -Manage facility asset condition data, lifecycle planning, and capital renewal pipelines across an assigned portfolio of buildings and systems. -Lead regional asset planning discussions with campus clients and Facilities Services units to identify operational priorities, lifecycle risks, and funding -Monitor deferred maintenance and renewal projects, providing status reporting and issue escalation to leadership. - Provide lifecycle and maintainability input during design reviews, construction coordination, and project closeout activities. (30% time)

Leads deferred maintenance remediation and capital renewal planning through ICAMP allocation programs. - Manages facility asset condition data, lifecycle planning, and capital renewal across campus buildings and infrastructure systems. Leads campus asset planning discussions with academic occupants, departmental leaders, and Facilities Services units to identify operational priorities, lifecycle risks, and funding opportunities. Coordinates asset integration in conjunction with complex backlog repair work and major mechanical/electrical/plumbing (MEP) priorities (e.g., chillers, boilers, substations, switchgear, roofing assemblies) with internal trade shops, Capital Projects / PD&C, and outside contractors. Monitors capital project milestones, escalates operational and lifecycle risks to senior management, and ensures minimal disruption to critical building occupants. (25% time)

Collaborates with leadership on space planning, design reviews, and capital improvement projects for facilities with complex needs. - Serves as the organizational technical expert for asset tracking, condition data, and predictive lifecycle models within the CMMS and ICAMP systems. Conducts complex field audits and engineering condition assessments across campus facilities to determine Remaining Useful Life (RUL), replacement logs, equipment degradation curves, and asset criticality. Reconciles physical installations against database registers, ensuring all newly commissioned capital assets are appropriately classified, barcoded, and mapped into recurring PM schedules prior to project closeout. (20% time)

Collaborates with leadership on design reviews, and capital improvement projects for facilities with complex needs. - Collaborates with campus and departmental leadership and facility occupants to evaluate and advise on space planning, capacity, and design allocations that accommodate non-routine systems, specialized research equipment, and hazardous materials management. Provides ongoing planning and maintainability coordination for construction, remodeling, and major alterations. Critiques and reviews contract documents, engineering specifications, and architectural plans from outside consultants during design phases to ensure campus standards, maintainability, and code compliance are incorporated. Works with internal and external agencies and contractors in regarding existing contract terms and provides technical support to solicit or negotiate contract scopes of work. (15% time)

Budget Analysis & Resource Management - Analyze operational metrics to develop budgetary recommendations for management review. Evaluate spending trends and provide strategic guidance on the optimal allocation of material resources and contracted labor across reactive work orders, scheduled PMs, and deferred maintenance remediation projects. (5% time)

Coordinates safety, regulatory compliance, and emergency facilities operations. - Coordinates with multiple internal units and external regulatory agencies to ensure a safe, secure, and compliant facilities environment across the assigned portfolio. Reviews building management procedures and operating protocols; recommends and implements changes to ensure currency, relevance, and strict adherence to internal policies, environmental health & safety (EH&S) regulations, and state building codes. Coordinates emergency repairs during and after work hours. (5% time)
Required to hold valid driver's license, have a driving record that is in accordance with local policies/procedures, and/or enroll in the California Employer Pull Notice Program.
Thorough knowledge of facilities maintenance and administration.

Advanced knowledge in the areas of building space planning, codes, capacity, security, fire safety, organization and departmental principles and procedures involved in risk assessment and evaluating risks as to likelihood and consequences.
Advanced knowledge of architectural or engineering concepts.
Advanced skills in working collaboratively and influencing others.
Advanced knowledge and skill regarding specialized research needs in space planning and advanced skill to effectively translate needs to professional architects and engineers.
Advanced skill to multi-task and effectively prioritize large project work.
Advanced skills to assess processes or services to make improvements and in project management.
